reasoning: I read both sets' brief, roadmap, spec, architecture, pipelines, contract, tests, plan and todo, plus several packets from each (A: M1-T03 spine, M1-T05 split thicken; B: M1-T07 spine, M1-T15 split thicken). A is the leaner and more sound plan. Its RL decisions are well reasoned. The Snake agent gets a full-grid observation, because with only the 11 classic features it could at best tie the scripted snake (AD-04). Run length is a step budget, so repeated runs give the same curve (AD-18). The fish stage goes from one fish that sees everything to five fish that see only nearby things. A statistics method and a chart style are pinned in the design, not left to placeholder skills. Its first milestone trains a snake and lets you watch it, end to end. A's weaknesses are leftover superseded wording in the pipelines ("time-boxed", "the null-hypothesis-testing skill's test", "torch.load the state dict"), process narration inside AD-15 and AD-22, an oversized fish-tank milestone M3, and a Double DQN learner sized XS. B is thorough but bloated. Every stage is split into the same three milestones (train / baselines-curves-replay / study), so its M1 can't replay an agent. It builds a large two-sided core before any second world exists, and its studies take 10–16 hours, stretching the one-hour-per-environment limit. Its Snake bar is internally contradictory: the 11-fact agent must beat a scripted snake that reads the true game state, while the spec's own assumption says the agent "may only tie it". It also keeps stale "docs to rework / build waits for replan" text in the architecture. Its plan chains four DQN thicken tasks that each write a different file, uses task IDs out of order, and flags an import-linter gate problem that must be fixed before M1-T01 can pass. Every M1 packet repeats the 34-row PL-01 table, including hunt and self-play rows that M1 never builds.

strengths: Sound RL choices: Double DQN on a full-grid Snake observation (AD-04) that can actually beat the scripted snake; PPO with a squashed Gaussian action; one fully-seeing fish before five fish that see only nearby things
The statistics (AD-20) and chart style (AD-21) are pinned down, so the 'beats a baseline' claim can be checked
M1 is a real walking skeleton: train a snake, then record and watch a replay
Compact contract: one sample case and one fake per boundary; packets carry the frozen types they need
weaknesses: The pipelines keep superseded wording (time-boxed training, deferring to the skills, saving a state dict) that AD-15, AD-18, AD-20 and AD-21 replaced
Process narration inside design decisions (AD-15, AD-22) and a Replan notes section
M3 holds the whole fish stage (tank, PPO, two tank versions, the SB3 multi-fish adapter, sign-off), so it is lopsided against the other milestones
M1-T05 builds a full Double DQN learner with curve points and divergence handling, yet is sized XS

strengths: Very detailed spec, with worked Given/When/Then cases for every rule
A thorough contract: domain errors are typed and every boundary has sample cases
Ablation switches and a policy-gradient ladder are good teaching devices
Packets are self-contained, with the full frozen type set

weaknesses: Every stage splits into train / baselines-curves-replay / study milestones, which are horizontal layers; M1 can't replay an agent
Studies of 10–16 hours stretch the user's limit of about an hour of training per environment
The Snake bar is contradictory: EVAL-04 says the agent must beat a scripted snake that reads the true game state, while the spec's assumption says it may only tie
Stale process text ('Docs to rework', 'Nothing is built yet (M1 has 0 of 22 tasks done)') sits in the architecture
False serialization: the four DQN thicken tasks are chained though each writes its own file
Task IDs run out of order, and every M1 packet carries the 34-row PL-01 table
